suggestions.rationale: Secondary osteoarthritis is a recognized articular complication of Paget disease of bone, particularly where Paget-related bone enlargement or deformity alters mechanics at an adjacent joint. Consensus and review literature identify secondary osteoarthritis among important Paget complications. This supports focused research when osteoarthritis developed in a joint anatomically related to documented Paget involvement; it does not establish that Paget disease caused osteoarthritis at an unrelated joint or in an individual case without site-specific chronology and competing-risk review.

pathwayIntelligence.causalChain: Paget-related abnormal bone remodeling and deformity near a joint may alter joint mechanics and contribute to secondary degenerative osteoarthritis in that anatomically related joint.
developmentQuestions: Which bones and joints are involved by Paget disease on imaging?
Is the osteoarthritis located at a joint anatomically affected by adjacent Paget-related deformity or enlargement?
Did osteoarthritis develop or materially worsen after the Paget disease became clinically or radiographically established?
issuesToResolve: Age-related, post-traumatic, inflammatory, occupational, alignment, obesity, and other independent osteoarthritis risk factors
Whether the claimed osteoarthritis is anatomically remote from Paget involvement

evidenceGaps: Imaging and specialist records establishing Paget disease and the specific bones involved
Imaging confirming osteoarthritis in the anatomically related joint
Chronology of Paget-related deformity and osteoarthritis onset or progression
Documentation of trauma, alignment, age, weight, occupation, inflammatory disease, and other osteoarthritis risk factors
Qualified orthopedic or metabolic-bone assessment addressing the site-specific relationship in the individual case

sourceReferences.citation: Devogelaer JP, Bergmann P, Body JJ, et al.; Belgian Bone Club. Management of patients with Paget's disease: a consensus document of the Belgian Bone Club. Osteoporos Int. 2008;19(8):1109-1117. PMID 18504638
sourceReferences.note: Consensus review identifies secondary osteoarthritis among clinically important complications of Paget disease of bone. Supports a site-specific complication pathway, not automatic attribution of osteoarthritis at any joint.
